Name this leader of the Upper CanadaRebellion of 1837 and grandfather of the Canadian Prime Minister during World War II.

He ended a period of co-rule by killing his rivalNeoptolemus at a banquet. His effort to put Cleonymus on the throne of Sparta failed when heencountered unexpected resistance. He turned down an offer of the Macedonian throne to go toSicily, where he alienated the Greek cities despite his victories over the Carthaginians. The Romansrenamed the town of Maleventum to Beneventum after this man fought there on behalf of Tarentum. Earlier, he used elephants given to him by Ptolemy II to defeat the Romans at Heraclea andAsculum. He was killed trying to take Argos, when a woman flung a roof tile on him. Namethis leader of Epirus known for his costly victories against the Romans.

This event was threatened when U.J. Fields resigned and accused its leaders of corruption. Oneleader of this action phoned T.J. Jemison a few days after it began to ask about a similar event thathad taken place in Baton Rouge. Minneapolis Tribune reporter Carl Rowan uncovered a ploy to stopthis event by leaking rumors of its demise. It ended when the Supreme Court affirmed the ruling ofBrowder v. Gayle. This event was supported by the "National Deliverance Day of Prayer," and oneattempt to end it involved fining taxi drivers who charged under forty five cents a fare. The SCLCwas founded a month after this event ended, and it lasted 381 days despite bombings of E.D. Nixon andMartin Luther King. The arrest of Rosa Parks prompted what event which sought to endsegregation on the public transportation system of an Alabama city?

This country avoided a religious civil war by appointing a mediator, who threw his idols into awaterfall after spending a day and a night in his tent deciding it should become a Christian country.It became Lutheran when the Battle of Saudafell was lost by its last Catholic bishop, Jon Arason.According to legend, the first settler of this country threw two pillars into the water and built itscapital where they landed. During World War II it was bloodlessly invaded in Operation Fork by theUK, and declared itself a Republic in 1944. As a commonwealth, one third of its laws were recitedaloud each year by a "Law Speaker." Those laws were read at the meetings of its assembly, which claimsto be the oldest extant parliamentary institution, although its powers were diminished during this country's1262 to 1944 union with Norway. The Allthing meets in what island nation in the northAtlantic?

After independence, this country arrested Alice Lenshina, whose Lumpa Church had causeddeadly conflicts nationwide. Schoolteacher and failed mayoral candidate Edward Nkloso trainedpeople in rolling in a barrel and walking on their hands for this country's unofficial space programin the 1960s. This country's 1996 elections were boycotted by the UNIP after an amendment waspassed limiting the presidency to children of citizens, forcing a Malawi descended candidate out andensuring the victory of Frederick Chiluba. This country was led from independence to 1991 by a manwho developed a national "humanism" and cut off trade with his southern neighbor Rhodesia. For 10points, Kenneth Kaunda led what landlocked African country with capital at Lusaka.

News of the death of a prince of this name was withheld for three days out of fear until a smallchild was finally picked to relate it. That prince's death was a direct cause of The Anarchy andoccurred on the White Ship, leaving Henry I heirless. A king of this name offered BuckinghamPalace to parliament after the Houses of Parliament burned down, and grew unpopular after givingonly timid support to the First Reform Bill. In addition to that "Sailor King," the second king ofthis name was nicknamed "Rufus" and was shot in the back by Walter Tyrrel in the New Forest. The thirdking of this name was originally a Dutch Stadtholder, and the first commissioned the Doomsday Book. For10 points, give this shared name of the king who ascendeded to the throne after the Glorious Revolutionand the one known as the conqueror after the Battle of Hastings.

This man wrote of a plan to rule 55 million, then 224 million, then 420 million people in his bookPhilosophy of the Revolution. This leader was prepared to accept the Rogers Plan to end his "war ofattrition." He greatly enhanced the power of the General Intelligence Directorate, and earlier, thisman founded a secret organization with Abd al-Hakim Amir, Zakaria Mohieddine, and his ownfuture successor. He attempted to resign after the Six-Day War but was refused. Name thisarchitect of the United Arab Republic who was succeeded by Anwar Sadat as President of Egypt.

This man's public works projects included the enneakrounos or Nine-Conduit Fountain. Afterthis man's death, his namesake dynasty was ended when his city was conquered by Cleomenes. Thisman was given 50 bodyguards after he intentionally wounded himself on his chariot; he subsequentlydrove out the Paraloi and Pediakoi parties. Hadrian finally finished the temple to Zeus started underthis man. This father of Hippias and Hipparchus captured the harbor of Megara and was a championof the hyperakrioi or Hillsmen, a group of landless people who had been absolved of their debts by Solon.name this Athenian tyrant who died in 527 BCE, helping unify Attica and set Athens on thepath to democracy.

This man was publicly inoculated for smallpox by Dr. Thomas Young in violation of the law.With his brothers, this man founded the Onion River Land Company. Late in his life, he publishedthe anti-Christian tract, Reason: the Only Oracle of Man. Governor William Tryon once put out aone hundred pound bounty for his arrest. This man was held prisoner by the British afterunsuccessfully attempting to take Montreal under General Philip Schuyler. He had earlier helpedBenedict Arnold capture Fort Ticonderoga. He threatened to join Canada if New York prevented theindependent statehood of Vermont. Name this leader of the Green Mountain Boys.

David Butler, the Irish commander of the Orel warship, fled from the forces of this man duringone siege. This man's "secret" of class warfare can be learned by climbing a hill named for him inSaratov. He left Vaska Us in charge of a city where he was elected gosudar so he could march onSamara. This man raided the Caspian settlements of Derbent and Baku before capturing Simbirsk.After his forces were defeated by Prince Baryatinsky, he unsuccessfully fled to the Don. Hesupposedly threw a Persian princess into the Volga, a tale popularized by an Alexander Glazunovcomposition titled for him. This man's namesake rebellion came to an end when Astrakhan fell in 1671. For10 points, name this Cossack who led a campaign against Tsar Alexis.

John Derbyshire wrote a novel about Chai, a former Red Guard member who becomes fascinatedwith this president, who was the subject of Gamaliel Bradford's essay "The Genius of Average". Hiswife was rumored to have had an affair with a secret service officer named James Haley, while hisnamesake son died from an infected blister from a tennis match played on the White House lawn.This man repeatedly vetoed the McNary-Haugen Farm Relief Act but did sign the restrictiveJohnson-Reed Immigration Act into law. He declared "the chief business of the American people isbusiness" and appointed J. Edgar Hoover head of the FBI. Before becoming president, he called out theMassachusetts militia to put down the Boston Police Strike. Name this successor to WarrenG. Harding.

During this period, authorities discovered some suspects on a farm owned by Michael Viger. Agroup active during this period demanded five hundred thousand dollars in gold, the reinstatementof 450 fired mail carriers, and a flight to either Cuba or Algeria. During this period, Paul Rose andFrancis Simard strangled to death a man using the religious chain he wore around his neck. Robert Bourassa appeared on television five minutes prior to a deadline in this event stating that hisgovernment would not negotiate, resulting in the retaliatory execution of Pierre LaPorte, who had beenkidnapped along with James Cross. The War Measures Act was enacted during this period by PrimeMinister Pierre Trudeau. Name this period of agitation by the FLQ in the namesake month in1970.

This man replaced the Marquis de Mondejar to put down a revolt in a campaign where his tutor,Don Luis de Quijada, was killed alongside him. This man's secretary may have found out about anaffair between Antonio Perez and Ana de Mondoza, the Princess of Eboli, leading to that secretary'smurder. This employer of Juan de Escobedo captured Namur after the Perpetual Edict was rejected by provinces like Zeeland. After his biggest victory, he led a raid on Tunis in 1573. Hecommanded the Spanish side alongside Italians like Giovanni Andrea Doria in a naval victory over forcesunder Ali Pasha in a battle where Miguel Cervantes was injured. Name this illegitimate sonof Charles V who won the Battle of Lepanto, not to be confused with a legendary lothario.

This man's son and namesake was killed by the Spanish on an ill-fated expedition led byLawrence Keymis. His book A Report of the Truth of the Fight About the Isles of Azores This LastSummer celebrated the heroic death of Sir Richard Grenville. This man went searching for ElDorado in Guiana and suffered a serious leg wound during the 1596 capture of Cadiz. Thisone-time owner of Durham House secretly married Elizabeth Throckmorton after the ascent of his rival,Robert Devereux. He was once imprisoned in the Tower of London for plotting to install Arabella Stuart onthe throne. This man sponsored an expedition that included the parents of Virginia Dare. Name this favorite of Queen Elizabeth who sponsored the Roanoke Colony.

A force assembled in this colony was turned back at the Battle of Kakamas. This colony wassubsequently invaded with battles at Swakopmund and Karibib. The rulers of this colony wereopposed by leaders such as Jakobus Marenga and Hendrik Witbooi in the Khaua-MbandjeryRebellion. This colony was the site of the Battle of Waterberg, which led to much of its nativepopulation being transferred to Shark Island. This colony, which was transferred to the British afterWorld War I, had been founded in 1882 by Adolf Luteritz. Identify this site of the Namaquaand Herero genocide, a Reich-held colony in present-day Namibia.

An attempt to avoid the expropriation of property belonging to these people by selling it into a"secret trust" for $1 was ruled an improper evasion of the Edmunds-Tucker Act. The legitimacy ofthese people's children was addressed in Cope v. Cope, and the swearing of an oath against being oneof these people as a prerequisite to vote was upheld in Davis v. Beason. Members of this group,including George Smith and Daniel Wells, engineered a test case of the 1862 Morrill Act, which ledthe Supreme Court to declare that "Laws are made for the government of actions, and while they cannotinterfere with mere religious belief and opinions, they may with practices." name thesepeople at the center of the 1879 Reynolds v. U.S. Case, one of many cases allowing the federal governmentto look askance at their practice of polygamy.

Janet Reno launched an investigation into this event following a confession of a bar owner namedLoyd Jowers that aired on ABC. The man responsible for this event was eventually found in Londonusing the name Ramon George Sneyd on a false passport. The Columbia Heights neighborhood ofWashington, D.C. Was largely destroyed in a riot instigated by followers of Stokely Carmichael in theaftermath of this event. Some people learned of this event in a speech that Robert Kennedy gave inIndianapolis. This event took place during a struggle between Mayor Henry Loeb and the city's sanitationworkers. This event took place at the Lorraine Motel in Memphis and followed the deliverance of the "I'veBeen to the Mountaintop" speech. Name this murder carried out by James Earl Ray.
Assassination of Martin Luther King, Jr.

A king from this dynasty put M.J. Crusenstople on trial, resulting in the pro-free speech Rabulistriots. Resistance to the establishment of this dynasty took the form of the Convention of Moss, whichinsisted that the May Constitution be retained as a condition of accepting its rule. A king from thisdynasty forced Frederick VI to sign new territory over to him at the Treaty of Kiel and patronizedthe construction of the Gota Canal. The founder of this dynasty was once implicated in the RennesPlot, and became the governor of Hanover and Bremen before being awarded the title of Prince ofPontecorvo. A member of this house who never came to the throne was approached by Heinrich Himmlerwith a rejected offer to surrender to the UK and US only, and later was killed alongside Andre-Pierre Serotby the Stern Gang. Name this dynasty of the diplomat Folke and Charles XIV, whoestablished it in Sweden after serving under Napoleon.

Through the Polish Ã©migrÃ© Philip Michael Newlenski, this man attempted to gain an audience with Sultan Abdulhamid II while a member of the Neue Freie Presse. This man was opposed by Israel Zangwill, who belonged to an organization that this man worked with that was headed by Albert Goldsmid. An early influence on this man's politics was his lifelong friend Reverend William Hechler. With Max Norday, this man established the Basel Program, through which the Russian faction shot down the Uganda Plan put forward by this man. This publisher of the newspaper Der Welt had a historic meeting with Kaiser Wilhelm II in Jerusalem. Name this publisher of The Jewish State, who was the first president of the World Zionist Organization and the father of Zionism.

The first major pretender to this title was considered so harmless that he was allowed to work as a diplomat to Great Britain and the United States. One holder of this title had a personal bodyguard led by Felix Salm-Salm. A future holder of this title initiated the scientific Novara Expedition, which engaged in revolutionary oceanographic research in the South Pacific and investigated coca plants. That holder of this title also created the New Virginia Colony, allowing disaffected ex-Confederates to settle in his country. The first holder of this title was overthrown under the Casa Mata Plan and was a co-leader of the Army of the Three Guarantees. The last holder was executed at the Hill of Bells after being captured in Queretaro along with his wife Carlotta. Name this position held by Augustin Iturbide and Maximilian von Habsburg.

William Maxwell and John Sullivan fought important delaying actions during this battle, the latter buying time for the arrival of reinforcements under Nathaniel Greene. This battle was directly preceded by the Battle of Cooch's Bridge. General von Knyphausen led the flanking attack that ended this battle, which was followed by a defeat for Anthony Wayne known as the Paoli Massacre. The Marquis of Lafayette was wounded at this battle, and due to bad intelligence the Americans thought General Howe's main attack would be aimed at Chadd's Ford. Name this September 1777 defeat for George Washington in Pennsylvania, which allowed the British to capture Philadelphia.

This nation is home to the Oku volcanic field, as well as Lake Monoun. The northeastern part of this nation is separated from the rest by the Adamawa Plateau. This nation's major river is the Sanaga, which empties into the Atlantic Ocean. Directly off the coast of this nation, but controlled by its southern neighbor, is the island of Bioko and its capital of Malabo. This nation's Lake Nyos underwent a limnic eruption in 1986, killing over a thousand people from asphyxiation with carbon dioxide. This nation has a strip of land that runs north into Nigeria, giving it access to Lake Chad. Name this former German colony in Africa, whose capital is Yaounde.

The original visitors to this place called themselves "Captain Ridley's shooting party." John Tiltman operated Hut 7 in this place. One organization in this place was satirically called "the Golf, Cheese and Chess Society," and F.H.W. Hawes won a contest in order to gain employment at this place. Thrasher and Sturgeon were names given to devices called FISH that were used here. This place was also home to devices named Bombe and Colossus, which were built by Gordon Welchman. One leader referred to this place as "my geese that laid the golden eggs". Also known as Station X, this placed produced Ultra which helped the navy win battles against Admiral Doenitz. Home to luminaries like Alan Turing, for 10 points name this site of the British effort to decrypt the German enigma machine.

This king was targeted by a poison dagger wielding assassin after his unsuccessful raid on the Levantine city of Qaqun, but managed to kill the assassin during the struggle. This king's seneschal, Luke de Tany, was killed while launching a surprise attack from a pontoon bridge. This king gathered information about corrupt local officials during a census called the "Hundred Rolls". This king employed the Savoyard architect James of Saint George, and built castles such as Beaumaris on the island of Anglesey. This king convoked the so-called "Model Parliament". After defeating both Dafydd ap Gruffydd [davith ap grifith] and his older brother Llywelyn, this king issued the Statute of Rhuddland, formally annexing Wales. This king also won the Battle of Falkirk. Name this English king, best known as the antagonist of William Wallace.

This leader headed the Casablanca Bloc, which sought greater international political integration. He's not Egyptian, but this member of the Akan ethnic group married a Coptic woman named Fathia Rizk. This leader lost support after passing the Preventive Detention Act, which legalized arrest without due process. This man defeated Joseph B. Danquah to attain his highest post. He was succeeded by Joseph Ankrah, who came to power in a coup staged while this man was visiting North Korea, and who banned this man's Convention People's Party. This organizer of the Positive Action Campaign led his nation to independence from Great Britain imposed price controls and other socialist policies and was noted for his strong support of Pan-Africanism. Name this man who led the Gold Coast to independence and was the first president of Ghana.

During this campaign, St. Czeslaw allegedly saved the city of Breslau by summoning a giant fireball. One battle during this campaign saw the death of Duke Henry the Pious. The pretext for this military campaign was the refuge given to Koten, leader of the Cumans. The main battle of this campaign saw the successful use of catapults to disperse harassing crossbowmen, considered a breakthrough in artillery tactics. That battle ended with knights forced to retreat into a swamp to escape a double envelopment, where many were bogged down and killed. In one of the target countries, this campaign marked the start of a period called the "tatarjaros", which saw the capital moved from Szekesfehervar to the more defensible Buda. After the battles of Legnica and Mohi ended in victory for general Subotai, this campaign ended because of a kurultai caused by the death of Ogedei. Name this 1241 campaign in which Batu Khan invaded the continent west of Asia.

Ahmad Ibn Fartuwa was a chronicler of this kingdom's most illustrious king. The queen mother in this kingdom was called a magira and often held great power behind the throne. Most of the knowledge about this kingdom comes from the Diwan or Girgam, which is a royal chronicle discovered by Heinrich Barth. An important capital was located at Ngaxzargamu. One important mai or king of this nation named Hummay converted it to Islam and founded the Sayfawa dynasty. Another defeated the Tuareg, built a hostel in Mecca for pilgrims from this kingdom, and established diplomatic relations with the Ottomans. Idris Alooma ruled it while the neighboring Songhai empire was collapsing. Name this African Empire centered near Lake Chad and composed of two states.

This regime notably persecuted many jazz musicians, causing stars such as Mulatu Astatke to leave the country. This government came to power after rumors that the Armed Forces Coordinating Committee under Alem Zewde Tessema was in cahoots with the fallen aristocracy. One rebellion against this regime was led by a group nicknamed the "Ihapa". The first leader of this government was Aman Andom, who was quickly executed and replaced by Tafari Benti. This regime originally consisted of approximately 120 soldiers under the rank of major. General Mohammad Samatar led an invasion of this regime's homeland on behalf of President Siad Barre. This regime was violently opposed by the Tigrayan People's Liberation Front and its slogan was "Land to the Tiller". Name this regime led by Mengistu Haile Mariam, a Marxist-Leninist junta that overthrew Hailie Selassie and ruled Ethiopia from 1974-1987.

During this event, a medical mistake made at Kings County Hospital led to the unnecessary death of one victim, though that error fueled the agitators because they cited it as evidence that local medical care was substandard. A picture of one man holding an open umbrella at a police car was run by a local newspaper during this event in a biased attempt to show that unrest was being caused by different types of people. Lemnick Nelson was accused of stabbing an Australian graduate student during it, and it was touched off when the leading car of a motorcade killed a seven year old boy named Gavin Cato. The killing of Yankel Rosenbaum was the peak of violence during this event that saw West Indians and African Americans burn and loot Jewish shops and homes. Name this 1991 riot in a namesake district of New York City that gained notoriety after Al Sharpton participated in a march during it.

This unit, which sunk the destroyer Ciscar, had tanks with a St. Andrew's cross painted on the top as an identification mark. Eighty-six personnel involved with this unit were disguised as people on a leisure cruise so they could be secretly transported on the Usaramo, as part of Operation Magic Fire, which was also called Operation Guido. This unit had a heavily-armored support contingent nicknamed "beekeeper". This unit was among the first to use tactics suggested by the Italian theorist Giulio Douhet. This unit saw action against a general nicknamed "The Peasant" at the Battle of Jarama. This unit was commanded by Hugo Sperrle and fought in support of General Mola. Best known for pioneering carpet bombing and inflicting civilian casualties on Guernica, for 10 points name this German air unit that helped the Nationalists during the Spanish Civil War.

One member of this dynasty replaced his bodyguard with American veterans of Young's Scouts after nearly being killed with poisoned coffee. Belligerent doormen denied its emissaries access to the Second Hague Conference, forcing it to finally accept the Treaty of Eulsa. Mary Scranton's education reforms and Horace Allen's diplomacy were due to the notable political efforts of one queen of this house, whose family was sheltered for a year by Karl von Weber in a foreign embassy. The March 1st Movement erupted just after the death of one this dynasty's last rulers, whose aforementioned wife was brutally dismembered scattered throughout the forest behind its palace by lackeys of Miura Goro. This dynasty's modernizing Gabo Reforms followed a revolt against the yangban aristocracy by bamboo-wielding peasants, the Donghak Rebellion. The husband and son of the slain Queen Min were the last rulers of this dynasty prior to Japanese annexation. Sunjong and Gojong ruled, what successor of the Goryeo and final dynasty of Korea?

According to one account from this battle, Colonel William Robinson's forces were the first to be shot at, and a flanking action by Thomas Jessup was beaten back after initial success at the start of this battle. One of the opposing commanders at this battle was captured after soldiers on the opposite side pretended to be his own troops. That commander, Phineas Riall was also the commander at the battle that preceded this one, the Battle of Chippawa. The "hero" of this battle, James Miller led a successful charge to capture artillery. The two American commanders at this battle were badly wounded and forced to retire, and those two were Jacob Brown and Winfield Scott. Name this extremely bloody battle that took place near Niagra Falls during the War of 1812.

A medieval law named for this place served as the first English conveyancing act. In one treaty named for this place negotiated by Paulus Buys, Elizabeth I agreed to send an army under Robert Dudley to the Netherlands. In a synod named for this place, Henry I renounced investiture of bishops but demanded that they do homage to him prior to consecration in an agreement that was a model for the Concordat of Worms. This place is the namesake of a confession of faith for English-speaking Presbyterians. A 1931 statute named for this place formally established the Britih Commonwealth of Nations. This location also lends its name to a system of government marked by a strong legislature and a ceremonial head of state. Name this borough of London in which Edward the Confessor established an abbey, also home to Parliament.

This political movement founded a newspaper called "The New Diary", and it was also supported by the more established paper La Presna. Early leaders of this group include Carlos Fonseca, who was captured and executed. This group split into three factions over a theory called "GPP", but was reunited by the "Group of Twelve", who represented the Tercerist faction that would bring this group into power. Some activities against this organization were first exposed in the newspaper Al-Shiraa, published in Lebanon. This organization lost an election to the widow of a former member, Violeta Chamorro. This organization's namesake was abducted and killed for opposing Juan Sacasa, who was backed by the United States, much like the dynasty this group overthrew in 1979. Name this left-wing movement led by Daniel Ortega, the sworn enemies of the Contras in Nicaragua.

The Byzantine Empire lost control of this region after a general named Euphemius rebelled and invited an invasion from the south. During the 1848 revolutions, this region briefly became independent under the rule of Ruggeru Settimu. One group conquered this region by winning the Battle of Misilmeri, defeating the Zirid Dynasty. This region most recently lost its independence at the Battle of Gaeta. A naval conflict fought off the coast of this region was nicknamed the "Battle of the Counts" and ended in victory for Pedro III of Aragon. One conflict in this region was ended by the Peace of Caltabellotta. That conflict may have been instigated by Michael VIII Paleologus and began when women were allegedly molested by French troops. Name this Italian island region with a namesake Vespers.

One ruler of this dynasty fled after his regents Bogdan Filov and Prince Kyril were killed in aSoviet backed coup which eventually supported Georgi Dimitrov. That last Tsar of Bulgaria, Simeon,adopted this dynastic name as his surname and served as Prime Minister in the 2000s. Because ofQueen Maria II's marriage, the last four monarchs of Portugal were part of a line that merged theBraganzas with this house. The wife of Maximilian of Mexico and the Imperial overlord of the Congo Free State both hailed from this house, although its name was changed to "of Belgium." The headof another branch of this family was known as the "Uncle of Europe," although the descendents of EdwardVII changed this name. Name this ruling house of the United Kingdom which changed itsname to Windsor to avoid connotations of Germanicness during World War I.

The account of this battle by Ammianus Marcellinus suggests that the leader of one side eitherdrowned in a swamp or was burned up while his wounds were treated in a cabin. That leader refusedto wait for his nephew Gratian, who had defeated the Alamanni at Argentovaria the same year andwho essentially gained control of the entire empire as a result of this battle. One side in this battlesent phony peace envoys to delay for the arrival of his generals Alatheus and Saphrax. This battleresulted in the destruction of two-thirds of the Eastern Roman army, sparking the rise of Theodosius I. Ittook place in the province of Thrace, and saw Goths under Fritigern kill and defeat the forces of the RomanEmperor Valens. Name this disastrous 378 AD battle.

This leader allowed the Governor of Syria to assemble a navy and sack Cyprus. The Pledge ofRidwan was sworn after false rumors spread of the death of this man at the hands of the Quraysh.His forces won the Battle of Nikiou to prevent the Byzantine takeover of Egypt, and defeatedGregory the Patrician to take control of all of North Africa. He was elected by a committee of sixpeople appointed after his predecessor was stabbed. He was the first aristocratic convert to Islam,and his most lauded accomplishment was starting a committee to create and promulgate a standardversion of the Qur'an. This man was put under house arrest and assassinated by Egyptian rebels,indirectly causing the First Fitna. Name this predecessor of Ali, the third Caliph of Islam.

The New York Post was founded as a broadsheet for this party, and its other champions in thepress included William Cobbett writing as "Peter Porcupine" and dictionary editor Noah Webster.One leader of this party pardoned the tax rebel John Fries. The last serious candidates proposed bythis party were Richard Stockton and Rufus King. Fisher Ames, George Cabot, and TimothyPickering were members of a faction of this party called the Essex Junto, who were slandered as "bluelights" for their supposed disloyalty. It twice nominated Charles Cotesworth Pinckney for the presidency.One leader of this party suggested using bounties to promote production in "The Report on Manufactures,"and another appointed the Midnight Judges and signed the Alien and Sedition Acts. Namethis party of John Adams and Alexander Hamilton.

Fort Saint-Nicolas was built in this city after Louis XIV arrested most members of its city council.The Hotel de Ville, Hotel de Cabre and the Maison Diamantee survived the Nazi burning of its LePanier section after the Allied launch of Operation Dragoon. A "federalist revolt" in this city wassuppressed by Jean-Baptiste Carteaux and it was officially renamed "The City without a Name".The Palais Longchamp was constructed in this city to celebrate the opening of a canal that broughtwater from the Durance River. Alexander I of Yugoslavia was assassinated in this city in 1934. TheChateau d'If is off the coast of this most populous city in Provence. Name this French portcity on the Mediterranean which lends its name to the country's national anthem.

The deposed king of this state raised the Guelphic Legion for a never-launched attempt to retakethe throne. This state was defeated by France at the Battle of Hastenbeck, causing it to brieflywithdraw from the Seven Years War at the Convention of Klosterzeven. A king of this place fired the Gottingen Seven, a group including the Brothers Grimm. That king was Ernest Augustus, who becameking due to the Salic Law, which prevented Victoria from claiming its throne. Name thisGerman state whose monarchy had been joined to that of England since the rule of George I.

While still a youth, one of his guardians, Osbern, was killed in the same room in which he wassleeping. His reign was the last described in a chronicle by William of Jumieges. He signed the Truceof Abernathy with the Scottish king, Malcolm III Canmore. With French forces, this man defeatedan army led by Guy of Brionne at the Battle of Val-es-Dunes. This king formalized English feudalismwith the Oath of Salisbury. This man installed Lanfranc as Archbishop and was the half-brother ofOdo. He began construction on the Tower of London. This husband of Matilda of Flanders started anoverland campaign from Pevensey. This man benefited from a campaign launched by Tostig and HaraldHardraade. Name this commissioner of the Domesday Book and victor at the Battle ofHastings.

In 2005, this man's wife, a former member of the I Threes born Rita Anderson, attempted torebury him in Shashemene. As a child, his father kidnapped him from his home in Nine Mile. TheCIA may have attempted to assassinate him for his opposition to the JLP, but that didn't stop himfrom appearing at National Heroes Circle Stadium. This man helped fund Vincent Ford's SoupKitchen by giving Ford a largely undeserved co-writing credit. His early work "Simmer Down" wasdedicated to the "Rude Boys" he grew up with. He joined hands with political rivals Michael Manley andEdward Seaga during a 1978 "peace concert" where he and bandmates Bunny Wailer and Peter Tosh sang,"to think that jamming was a thing of the past". Name this Reggae artist of "No Woman, NoCry".

This place was destroyed by Horemhab, and stone from this place was used to constructHermopolis Magna. Royalty greeted the public at the Window of Appearance in this location. An artstyle named for this place was characterized by male figures with almost female breasts, and otherimages where small hands extend from the rays of a solar disk. Many buildings at this site weredesigned by an architect named Bek. This location lends its name to a series of letters betweenfigures like Amenhotep III and Kadashman-Enlil written in Akkadian. Four years after its founder's death,the royal court returned to Thebes. This place contains numerous portrait busts of Nefertiti and contains atemple to Aton. Name this capital of Akhenaten.

One man with this last name negotiated the Treaty of Wanghia, the first between the US andChina. It's not Jackson, but a man with this surname was the main American judge in theNuremberg Trials. A theologian with this surname was imprisoned for writing the Two-FoldCatechism in 1654 and was the leader of the English Unitarians. The best known man with thissurname wrote the 1814 History of the Expedition of Captains Lewis and Clark and sought to renewhis institution's charter four years earlier than needed, prompting a presidential veto. That same manwith this surname succeeded Langdon Cheves in a role where he clashed with a president who issued theSpecie Circular. Give this surname of Nicholas, a president of the Second Bank of the US.
